s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination shows dermoepidermal separation
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

differentials: chronic neutrophilic leukemia associated with csf3r mutation

shortlist.label: bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation and presence of milia are consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: lichen planus pemphigoides
shortlist.why_kept: Itchy, violaceous papules and plaques with dermoepidermal separation are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: pemphigus herpetiformis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erosions and milia, along with itchy lesions, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: atopic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Itchy, lichenified papules and plaques are common in atopic dermatitis, although the presence of dermoepidermal separation is less typical

shortlist.label: epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: The novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 and the presence of dermoepidermal separation suggest a possible connection to this disease

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation on histopathologic examination, milia in the superficial dermis, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, supports the diagnosis of epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: While bullous pemphigoid can present with similar skin lesions, the genetic testing results and specific histopathologic findings point more strongly towards epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

rejected.label: lichen planus pemphigoides
rejected.why: Lichen planus pemphigoides typically involves mucous membranes and has distinct histopathologic features not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: pemphigus herpetiformis
rejected.why: Pemphigus herpetiformis is characterized by intraepidermal blisters, which were not described in the histopathologic examination.

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: Atopic dermatitis does not typically present with dermoepidermal separation or the specific genetic variant identified in COL7A1.
